candidates.exact_span: EPA-approved test procedures (methods) for the analysis and quantification of pollutants or pollutant parameters, including for the purposes of compliance monitoring/DMR reporting, permit renewal applications, or any other reporting that may be required as a condition of this permit, shall be sufficiently sensitive.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a method must be 'sufficiently sensitive' for compliance monitoring/DMR reporting defines a precondition for using reported measurements in limit comparisons (A) and establishes a monitoring/reporting obligation tied to analytical method choice (B).

candidates.exact_span: A method is "sufficiently sensitive" when (1) the method minimum level (ML) of quantification is at or below the level of the applicable effluent limit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'applicable effluent limit' and the ML-versus-limit comparison determines whether a reported value is eligible for numeric exceedance evaluation (A) versus treated as a missing/non-comparable result when sensitivity is insufficient (C).

candidates.exact_span: or (2) if there is no EPA-approved analytical method with a published ML at or below the effluent limit (see table below), then the method has the lowest published ML (is the most sensitive) of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR Part 136 or required under 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapters N or O, for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter;
candidates.computation_change_reason: The fallback rule when no method meets the effluent limit governs which analytical method is required (B), whether numeric compliance comparison remains applicable at all (A), and how sub-limit or non-detect results are classified when limits are below achievable MLs (C).

candidates.exact_span: or (3) the method is specified in this permit or has been otherwise approved in writing by the permitting authority (EPA Region 6) for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permit-specified or authority-approved methods can override default sensitivity rules, changing which measurements count toward limit exceedance analysis (A) and which monitoring methods are obligatory (B).

candidates.exact_span: The Permittee has the option of developing and submitting a report to justify the use of matrix or sample-specific MLs rather than the published levels. Upon written approval by EPA Region 6 the matrix or sample-specific MLs may be utilized by the Permittee for all future Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether matrix/sample-specific MLs were approved changes the effective quantification threshold used in DMR reporting, altering limit-comparison eligibility (A), the scope of ongoing DMR obligations (B), and how no-result or below-threshold data are interpreted (C).

candidates.exact_span: Current EPA Region 6 minimum quantification levels (MQLs) for reporting and compliance are provided in Appendix A of Part II of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Appendix A MQLs supply the numeric thresholds for 'reporting and compliance'; different readings of which MQL applies change enforceable comparison points (A), required reporting sensitivity (B), and classification of results that fall below MQL (C).

candidates.computation_change_reason: Identification of pollutants for which no method can achieve the effluent limit affects whether numeric exceedance comparison is applicable (A) versus whether missing or non-quantifiable results reflect a documented no-comparison state rather than a violation (C).
